why: Long replies bury the trailing detail -- a question that was asked, a step still on the person -- and a real heading is the only thing that survives skimming. Declared in this person's individual set 2026-09-13, moved to universal 2026-09-14 as next-steps-after-commit, and consolidated 2026-09-15 into the-boildown along with five other closing-section practices, under a renamed heading. The mechanism is tools/precedent_reply_check.py, which checks whatever a source declares and has no requirements of its own. Split from the archive-sentence requirement below 2026-09-17: the heading stays a real, blocking requirement -- it is what makes the rest of this list findable -- independent of whether the archive sentence, now advisory, is present.

2026-09-20: a reply said 'no open work is blocking either way' in its own next-steps bullet and then closed with "Don't archive this session" -- the two cannot both be true, and nothing caught it before the person did. The advisory require_one_of above only checks that ONE of the two fixed sentences is present; it has no way to notice that the reply also asserts the opposite of the one it picked. Unlike the archive verdict itself -- deliberately left a judgment call, per the-boildown's own Install section, because no script can tell a real reason from a content-free recap -- a reply is never allowed to assert both halves of the same contradiction at once, whatever the real state is, so this one is blocking rather than advisory. Narrow on purpose: it does not try to verify the verdict is CORRECT, only that the reply does not talk itself out of its own answer. Second incident, same day: a reply's own Boildown bullet said "PR #165 merged... -- nothing left to do there" (scoped to that one closed PR) and correctly closed with "Don't archive this session" because an unrelated question was still open elsewhere -- the flat match had no notion of scope, so a per-item "nothing left to do" read identically to a whole-session one. Fixed by excluding an immediately-following scope qualifier (there / on it,that,this / for it,that,this) from both patterns in this entry, same family as the double-quote-citation exemption above it: a phrase scoped away from the whole session is not asserting the opposite of the verdict, any more than a quoted citation is.
